extracted.intended_audience: state militia and National Guard officers, adjutants general, War Department officials, military/government attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: A compilation of legal holdings and interpretive guidance about pay, allowances, equipment issuance, uniforms, administrative procedures, and property accountability for State militias and the National Guard under early 20th-century U.S. statutes (primarily the militia acts of January 21, 1903, March 1, 1889, February 18, 1909, and related appropriations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant surgeon rank pay entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: An assistant surgeon of a State National Guard who has the rank of captain either by appointment or by advancement by operation of law after five years' service in grade of first lieutenant is entitled, while engaged in the service specified in sections 14 or 15 of the act of January 21, 1903, to the pay of the rank of captain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies where rank exists either by appointment or automatic advancement; pay entitlement tied to performance of duties under specified statutory sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on differential enlisted pay for horse hire
rubrics_metrics.description: A disbursing officer cannot legally pay enlisted men at a different rate of pay from that allowed enlisted men of the Regular Army for the purpose of covering the hire of horses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disallows local pay-rate deviations by disbursing officers for horse-hire; regular Army rates govern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extra pay when officer provides own mount
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer of the Organized Militia below grade of major whose duty requires him to be mounted and who provides himself a mount is entitled to the same extra pay for the same period as an officer of the Regular Army would be entitled to under the act of May 11, 1908.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the State furnishes a mount from horses it has hired under its allotment under section 1661 R.S., the officer is not entitled to extra pay for being mounted.

rubrics_metrics.name: No reimbursement for personal provision of mounts
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no provision of law authorizing reimbursement in full of amounts claimed by militia officers who have provided their mounts at their own expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officers who purchase mounts themselves generally cannot recover full claimed amounts from federal funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: No longevity/increased pay for state militia commissioned service
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer of the National Guard is not entitled to increased pay for length of service when the service has been rendered as a commissioned officer of the Organized Militia of a State, Territory, or District of Columbia; prior Regular Army service does not entitle Organized Militia officers to longevity pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service in State Organized Militia does not count toward federal longevity pay increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment from sec.1661 funds for preparatory camp duty
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer ordered by the governor to a camp ground to make preparation for reception of troops and who submits accounts with muster and pay rolls as required may have the charge paid from funds allotted under sec.1661, R.S., as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural compliance (muster/pay rolls) important to charge to sec.1661 allotment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay during board service after maneuvers
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer who served as a member of a board to assess damages as a result of joint maneuvers is entitled to the pay and allowances of his rank while his organization remained on duty and after its return to home station until the board completed its labors; compensation payable from Army appropriation act (e.g., June 12, 1906 'Barracks and quarters' item).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entitlement extends beyond formal return until board duties complete; specific appropriation lines may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: No pay while on leave during encampment
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer on duty at encampment is not entitled to pay while on leave under proper orders during a portion of the period while encampment is in progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave status during encampment bars pay for the leave period despite overall encampment involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired-list officers not paid unless recommissioned
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer of the retired list of the militia placed on active duty in connection with camps of instruction, competitions, etc., without being recommissioned on the active list in the Organized Militia, is not entitled to pay under section 15 of the act of January 21, 1903.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommissioning onto active list is prerequisite for pay under section 15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age/physical fitness limitation on pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress intended that an officer ceases to be able after age 64 to encounter the hardships of active field service; department not obliged to compensate persons not able-bodied or disqualified by age/physical disability from rendering efficient service in camps/instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: War Department may describe classes of disabled persons to whom state or congressional funds will not be paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation covers pay of range personnel for rifle practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of June 22, 1906 (promoting rifle practice) makes provision covering pay of 'pitmen,' 'markers,' 'caretakers' etc., for work on ranges built and maintained by a State on leased ground with state funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States sending teams can contribute from sec.1661 apportionment; remainder properly chargeable to U.S. and payable from Army appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Muster for travel time as basis for payment
rubrics_metrics.description: If battalion members were mustered for pay by a Regular officer for the period consumed in returning to their home station, such muster constitutes a basis for payment for travel days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper muster by Regular officer for travel period is required to obtain payment for travel time.

rubrics_metrics.name: No pay during illness en route post-match
rubrics_metrics.description: A member of a State rifle team who became sick while enroute home and was hospitalized is not entitled to pay during his illness and up to arrival at home because law limits pay to period in which militia are engaged in 'actual field or camp service of instruction.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right to pay strictly tied to statutory definition of 'actual field or camp service of instruction.'

rubrics_metrics.name: No disbursing-officer authority to pay heirs absent demand
rubrics_metrics.description: If a soldier participating in a camp died before signing the roll and no demand has been made by legal representatives, the act of June 30, 1906 vests no jurisdiction in the disbursing officer of the Army to make payment to heirs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims/payment to heirs require statutory or procedural basis; disbursing officer lacks blanket authority in such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory supply of new-type small arms and ammunition to Organized Militia
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of March 2, 1907 directs that rifles of new types and ammunition adopted for the Regular Army shall be furnished to the Organized Militia; statute is mandatory and leaves no discretion to Secretary of War regarding incidents of issue and exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes requirement that exchange of ammunition suited to old-type rifles must be at expense of United States; Secretary must accept state-purchased old-model ammunition and issue round-for-round suitable ammunition for new-type arms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on authority to rearm without appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 13 of the act of January 21, 1903 may have been already executed and thus functus officio; not sufficient authority to warrant rearming the militia without cost to appropriation under section 1661 R.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rearming actions must be supported by available appropriation authority; historical execution of statutory authority can limit later actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of arms issued based on militia strength at effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of magazine arms to be issued to a State or Territory under section 13 is determined by the strength of its Organized Militia as authorized on January 21, 1903 (the date militia law became effective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation based on census/strength at statutory effective date, not later fluctuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expense of issue/return haulage paid by U.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: Expenses of hauling arms to be issued to a State and of hauling those to be returned to the United States between the railway depot or nearest steam-boat dock and the State storehouse are to be paid by the United States from the appropriations made, and arms to be returned are to be accepted by the United States where they are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Logistics costs between depot/dock and state storehouse borne by US appropriation lines specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ammunition issuance tied to instruction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction in target practice is an essential condition to the free issue of ammunition to the National Guard under section 21 of the act of January 21, 1903; ammunition cannot be issued free merely for maneuvers though incidental instruction may occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost of ammunition used in maneuvers may be charged against state's allotment under sec.1661; appropriation intended for 'armament and equipment' includes ammunition but has restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate funds for specialized ammunition and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Seacoast artillery ammunition for use in instruction at forts may be lawfully expended from fortification bill funds when not inconsistent with their purpose, and may also be charged to a State's allotment under sec.1661 with the governor's proper requisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of fortification funds vs. state's allotment depends on purpose and proper requisition/consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional vs. Executive authority over uniforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Constitution vests Congress with power to provide for organizing, arming, and disciplining the militia, it does not give authority to prescribe uniforms (left to the States); however Congress may impose conditions when making gratuitous issues of uniform clothing (e.g., prohibit use of distinctive Regular Army marks), and this power belongs to Congress (not the Executive) absent statutory authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive cannot unilaterally prescribe or modify distinctive marks without legislative authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campaign badges as stores/supplies and issue limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaign badges constitute stores and supplies within the meaning of section 17 of the act of January 21, 1903 and may be issued to governors for the use of their Organized Militia as part of the uniform; medals procured out of Regular Army funds cannot be furnished to a cadet battalion not part of the Organized Militia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between legitimate recipients (Organized Militia) and entities not authorized to receive Army-funded medals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on supply/use of penalty envelopes
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalty envelopes cannot lawfully be supplied to State or Territorial authorities for discretionary use; they may be used when official information is called for by the War Department in replying, and adjutants general making required reports/returns under section 12 of the militia act may use them; officers who are not 'officers of the United States Government' may not use them for organization/equipment correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain State officials acting as agents of War Department (e.g., as Quartermaster agent) may use penalty envelopes; users bear criminal liability for misuse; disbursing officers may use penalty envelopes for specific official business but not free registration; banks cannot be furnished penalty envelopes for private use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telegraph costs charged to state allotment
rubrics_metrics.description: Telegrams sent by militia officers to the War Department should be paid from the allotment to the State from section 1661 R.S., not from general appropriations for carrying on the business of the General Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational communications costs generally borne from state allotments rather than central appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required routing of disbursing-officer correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: A disbursing officer's correspondence with the Secretary of War on matters pertaining to duties as an officer of the National Guard should be through the adjutant general of the State as required by War Department Circular No. 62, series 1906.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative routing requirements must be observed; direct contact is improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commanding general control over camp intoxicant sales
rubrics_metrics.description: The commanding general of a Department, during exclusive occupation of a State maneuver camp ground, is barred by the act of February 2, 1901 from permitting sale of intoxicating liquors thereon and may eject persons attempting such sales; he should not interfere with canteens established/maintained under State authority on National Guard camp premises during joint encampment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing federal exclusive occupation prohibition with State-authorized on-premises canteens; enforcement discretion limited by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: District of Columbia militia commissioning and status
rubrics_metrics.description: The active militia of the District of Columbia constitutes the 'Organized Militia' within meaning of section 3 of act of January 21, 1903; brigadier general and brigade staff should be commissioned under the act of March 1, 1889 and other officers commissioned as National Guard of the District per statutory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretive guidance reconciling earlier act (1889) with 1903 militia act for commissioning and organizational status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to disband understrength companies
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 18 of the act of March 1, 1889, the commanding general of the militia of the District of Columbia may disband or consolidate a company that for 90 days has contained less than minimum enlisted numbers or is found on inspection to be below proper standard of efficiency and may grant honorable discharges to supernumerary officers and noncommissioned officers produced by consolidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority limited to shown statutory scope and does not extend to Naval Militia; actions should be lawful and may be recommended for sanction by Secretary of War.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of medical boards for retirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 20 of the act of February 18, 1909 provides for retirement for physical disability, and absent a statutory requirement that the board be appointed by the President or Secretary of War, the commanding general of the District National Guard may appoint the medical board provided for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegated appointment authority to local commanding general unless statute specifies higher appointing authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory power for District National Guard composition and commissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 11 of the act of February 18, 1909 vests power in the President to issue regulations for the National Guard of the District of Columbia (including composition of medical department); an officer holding commission in one department may be commissioned in another in same grade and date under section 76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presidential regulations determine organizational composition and permit cross-department commissioning per statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limits of leave under act of March 1, 1889
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 49 of the act of March 1, 1889 entitles officers and employees of the United States and of the District who are Guard members to leave without loss of pay on all days of any parade or encampment ordered under the act; this section is limited to the District's National Guard and does not extend to State National Guard units generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits include nonretroactivity and specific definitions of 'parade' and 'encampment'—some activities (e.g., rifle range duty) may not qualify for messenger pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: No duplicate pay from different appropriations for same period
rubrics_metrics.description: If District troops are paid out of funds obtained under section 14 of the act of January 21, 1903, they are not entitled for the same period to pay provided in the District appropriation bill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoids double compensation from overlapping appropriations; payment source governs entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campaign badge entitlement and procurement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the District National Guard are entitled to campaign badges under the same conditions as Army officers; badges for enlisted men may be included in issues, but badges for commissioned officers should be obtained by purchase; commanding general determines whether service entitles wearing the badge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific procurement practice: enlisted badges issued, officer badges purchased; entitlement determined by commanding general's factual determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for United States property and recoupment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a National Guard officer fails to account for United States property for which he is alleged accountable, the commanding general may recommend stoppage of pay to recoup; Secretary of War may suspend payments pending action, and if judgment obtained cannot be satisfied, report to Secretary for further measures; commanding general remains solely responsible for property until properly relieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural steps: local action first, report to Sec. of War, and continued local accountability in the interim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property accountability evidence and certificate use
rubrics_metrics.description: Because property accountability in the District National Guard is assimilated to the Regular Army system, similar rules of evidence and higher standards of performance apply; officers may be permitted to give testimony in the form of certificates similar to those required of Regular Army officers in like circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits use of standardized officer certificates for property accountability testimony to meet higher evidentiary standards.
